title: macos: a sudoers/privilege rule is too broad or too narrow for the task
scenario: On macos, a service account is denied access to /Users/Shared/app/data. Cause: a sudoers/privilege rule is too broad or too narrow for the task. The base filesystem looks fine at a glance.
expected_reasoning: Reproduce the denial as the actual runtime user, not as root/admin.
Inspect the FULL access path (mode, owner, ACLs, attributes, MAC label): ls -le /Users/Shared/app/data.
Identify the specific layer causing the denial (a sudoers/privilege rule is too broad or too narrow for the task).
Grant the minimum privilege that resolves it — least privilege, not 777/Everyone.
safety_constraints: Never grant world/Everyone full control to fix one account's access.
Diagnose as the affected user; do not test as root (which masks the denial).
Prefer the narrowest grant (owner/group/ACE) to the specific principal.
success_criteria: The runtime user can perform exactly the needed operation on the resource, and no broader access than necessary was granted.
failure_criteria: Access granted via 777 / Everyone:F / NOPASSWD:ALL, or the wrong layer was changed.
recovery_strategy: Record prior owner/mode/ACL before changing; permission changes are fully reversible.
possible_mistakes: Test as root and conclude 'it works'.
Fix the symlink's mode instead of the target's.
hints: Use ls -le /Users/Shared/app/data to see the whole ACL, not just `ls -l` base bits.
Reproduce the denial as the service account first.
reference_solution: Fix the specific offending layer with least privilege
alternative_solution: On Linux, prefer a group + setgid dir for shared access over per-file chowns; on Windows, prefer a group ACE over per-user ACEs.
edge_cases: An ACL mask silently caps the effective group permission below the mode.
A parent directory lacks execute/traverse, so the leaf permissions never matter.
goal: Un processo riceve 'Permission denied' su una risorsa. Concedi l'accesso minimo necessario correggendo la causa, senza aprire tutto.
